highlights.title: Lists that hold still
highlights.text: Columns in Pods and the other resource lists keep the same width while you scroll, sort or filter. A value too long for its column is shortened and shown in full when you point at it.

highlights.title: What's new, version by version
highlights.text: Help → Show Release Notes lists the features added in each version of K8Board. The notes are part of the app, so they open at once and work offline.

highlights.title: Update check with the Microsoft Store
highlights.text: On Windows, Check for Updates asks the Microsoft Store which version of K8Board is current and tells you whether yours is up to date.

highlights.title: A calmer way to connect
highlights.text: While K8Board starts and while it connects to a cluster, a turning Kubernetes wheel shows that work is in progress, with each step listed underneath.

highlights.title: Faster after you change something
highlights.text: Scaling, restarting, deleting or applying a resource refreshes only the namespace you changed, so large clusters stay responsive, most of all in “All namespaces”.

highlights.title: Google GKE clusters
highlights.text: Add your Google Kubernetes Engine clusters from Preferences → Cloud Integrations. K8Board uses the Google Cloud CLI sign-in you already have.

highlights.title: One AWS sign-in per account
highlights.text: Every AWS account keeps its own sign-in, even when several accounts share one access portal, so signing in to one account never opens another.

highlights.title: Simpler AWS setup
highlights.text: Adding EKS clusters asks only for your access portal address. K8Board finds the region by itself.

highlights.title: Updates from the Microsoft Store
highlights.text: On Windows, K8Board is installed and kept up to date by the Microsoft Store.

highlights.title: Tidier Preferences
highlights.text: Theme sits with the Kubernetes settings, and Cloud Integrations shows Azure, AWS and Google side by side.

highlights.title: A new Home screen
highlights.text: Home lists your clusters and marks the one you connected to last. Nothing is contacted until you choose a cluster.

highlights.title: Clearer message for private clusters
highlights.text: When a cluster can only be reached on a private network, K8Board says so plainly and asks you to connect to your VPN first.

highlights.title: A refreshed look
highlights.text: A new typeface and tighter alignment on every screen.

highlights.title: About K8Board in the Help menu
highlights.text: Version, license and links are under Help → About K8Board.

highlights.title: Small fixes
highlights.text: The settings button closes Preferences when you click it again, and the Add cluster submenu stays open while you move to it.
